text_blocks.snippet: Numbness, tingling, and nerve pain in the hands and feet can be a lingering symptom of COVID-19, sometimes persisting for weeks or months after the initial infection. This condition, known as peripheral neuropathy, may be caused by the virus itself or by the body's immune response.
snippet_highlighted_words: Numbness, tingling, and nerve pain in the hands and feet can be a lingering symptom of COVID-19, sometimes persisting for weeks or months after the initial infection

list.title: Neuropathy:
list.snippet: COVID-19 can lead to nerve damage, resulting in symptoms like numbness, tingling, and pain in the extremities, particularly the hands and feet.
Immune Dysfunction: The body's immune system may mistakenly attack nerve cells, leading to inflammation and damage.
Hemodynamic Effects: COVID-19 can affect blood flow, potentially causing ischemia (reduced blood flow) to the nerves, which can damage them.

list.title: Lingering Effects:
list.snippet: Some individuals experience these nerve-related symptoms for extended periods after their initial COVID-19 diagnosis.

list.title: Research:
list.snippet: Studies suggest that COVID-19 can cause various sensory neurological issues, including numbness and tingling.
